items.purpose: Cover banner illustration (Slide 01): one composite wave separating into single-frequency sine waves and resolving into a row of frequency lines
items.prompt: Technical schematic illustration with magazine-editorial restraint. Crisp uniform 1.5px lines on an implied measured grid, right angles and precisely drawn curves, elements reduced to essential schematic forms — waveforms, tick marks, anchor dots, thin vertical bars. A very subtle grid in deep blue #123B63 at 6% opacity sits behind everything; a thin horizontal baseline rule runs across the lower third. Flat, no shading, no gradients, no glow, no perspective, no paper texture beyond a faint 5% grain. Deliberate alignment to invisible columns with generous gutters, one dominant focal movement reading left to right, generous calm negative space above. Background is paper white #FFFFFF with the pale field #F2F4F7 filling only the lower band. Composition, in three stages across the width: on the left third, one dense composite waveform in teal #2E7D7B drawn as a single continuous line with irregular peaks; in the middle third, that line separates into four evenly stacked smooth single-frequency sine waves, each a clean teal line with increasing frequency from top to bottom, each with small tick marks on its own short axis; on the right third, the stack resolves into a row of nine thin vertical bars of decreasing height in brick red #C2452D standing on the baseline rule, like an amplitude spectrum, with small anchor dots at their tops. Two thin brick-red arrows, drawn as plain hairlines, mark the transitions between the three stages. Composed as a 2389x1024px wide banner image for local use, its left and right edges kept calm so the picture can bleed off the page edge; no interior area is reserved for overlay text. NO text of any kind anywhere in the image — no letters, numbers, signs, watermarks, labels, units, axis names, or written symbols. Color values (HEX codes like #123B63) and color names are rendering guidance only — do NOT display HEX codes, color names, or palette labels as visible text anywhere in the image.
